comments.author: Michael Dizon
comments.content: Just a heads-up, this won’t be compatible with the Chinese region. TP-Link Tapo — best simple replacement for Xiaomi This would be my first choice for home CCTV in the Philippines. Tapo says its device-sharing system works through a TP-Link account, and TP-Link support specifically states that device sharing is normally not restricted by the country or region of the family member. It’s best to hold off on purchasing Xiaomi CCTV until the company addresses this issue. You might not be able to determine the price of a camera based on its region. For example, some people in China might buy region-specific cameras, while others in the Philippines might do the same. Trust me, many people purchase CCTV online, and sometimes those come from China. The problem is the company. Since most of them are made in China, if TP-Link has no issues, then go for that brand. Sorry, this is my honest opinion. To ensure everything works smoothly, it would be great if all dealers could make it clear in the letter that your Mi apps are set to the Chinese region. The CCTV won’t function correctly otherwise. This seems to be an internal issue within the company. Consider Apple; their iPhones and iPads are designed to work seamlessly in any country.
